newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mass layoffs down in September from year ago.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mass layoffs down in September from year ago.

text.p: The number of U.S. workers who lost their jobs in mass layoffs declined in September to 498 from 684 in September 1995, the Labor Department said Wednesday.

The report by the department's Bureau of Labor Statistics, which is based on a month's data of initial claims for unemployment benefits, is the first monthly measure of layoffs that involve at least 50 workers at a single establishment.
Unlike the department's quarterly layoff reports, which count only those mass layoffs lasting longer than 30 days, the monthly series includes layoffs of less than 30 days as well.

As a result, the number of mass layoffs in three monthly reports will be greater than the number of layoffs reported in a quarterly report, the department said. It has not yet issued its quarterly report for the third quarter.

In the third quarter, monthly short- and long-term mass layoffs, including September's 498, totaled 2,870, up from 2,816 in the second quarter and 2,792 in the three months ended September 1995, the department said. In the second quarter of 1996, 44 percent of the mass layoffs lasted more than a month, it said.
Manufacturing industries accounted for 231, or 46 percent, of September's mass layoffs, down from 355 in September 1995.
Mass layoffs in non-manufacturing industries fell to 211 in September from 281 in September 1995, it said.
